units.text: Neuronal signaling is best understood as a coordinated set of structures, processes, and changing conditions. Membranes and channels make electrical excitability possible. Axons and their supporting glia shape the delivery of signals. Synapses translate activity between cells, and synaptic plasticity alters how future signals are handled. Circuits combine these mechanisms to support adaptive behavior. A precise explanation preserves the distinction between a cell and its parts, between a structure and an event, and between a general mechanism and a particular example.
